title: Moncrieff et al. 2022 umbrella review of serotonin and depression

claims.title: The review evaluated major lines of serotonin-depression evidence
claims.detail: Moncrieff et al. 2022 reviewed evidence from areas including serotonin metabolite studies, receptor studies, transporter studies, tryptophan depletion, SERT gene association, and gene-environment interaction research in relation to depression.

claims.title: The review reports no consistent support for a simple serotonin-deficiency account
claims.detail: The review concluded that the main bodies of evidence did not consistently show that depression is caused by lower serotonin concentrations or reduced serotonin activity.

claims.title: The review concerns the simple chemical-imbalance formulation
claims.detail: The review primarily bears on the claim that depression is caused by a simple serotonin deficiency; it does not by itself rule out more complex roles for serotonin in mood regulation, treatment response, stress sensitivity, or neural plasticity.

claims.title: Umbrella-review evidence is limited by the quality and heterogeneity of included studies
claims.detail: The review synthesizes prior reviews and studies with varied populations, measures, and designs, so its conclusions depend on the quality and comparability of the included evidence base.

title: Jauhar et al. 2023 response discussing serotonin evidence after Moncrieff et al.

claims.title: The response argues that serotonin mechanisms can remain clinically relevant
claims.detail: The response argues that rejecting a simplistic low-serotonin theory does not eliminate possible serotonin involvement in depression or antidepressant response.

claims.title: The response emphasizes complexity rather than a single-deficit model
claims.detail: The response frames serotonergic mechanisms as part of a broader neurobiological system involving receptor subtypes, plasticity, stress response, and treatment effects rather than as a single static deficiency.

claims.title: The response does not establish serotonin deficiency as the primary cause
claims.detail: The response defends the relevance of serotonergic biology but does not by itself provide direct causal proof that major depressive disorder is primarily caused by low serotonin.

title: Cipriani et al. 2018 network meta-analysis of antidepressant efficacy

claims.title: Antidepressants were more efficacious than placebo over short-term acute treatment
claims.detail: Cipriani et al. 2018 reported that all included antidepressants were more efficacious than placebo for adults with major depressive disorder in short-term acute treatment trials.

claims.title: The analysis compares treatment efficacy and acceptability
claims.detail: The network meta-analysis compared multiple antidepressants on acute response and acceptability, drawing on randomized controlled trials.

claims.title: Treatment efficacy does not directly prove the untreated cause of depression
claims.detail: Evidence that antidepressants improve symptoms does not logically establish that depression is caused by deficiency in the neurotransmitter system targeted by those drugs; drug mechanism and disease etiology can differ.

claims.title: Trial evidence is mostly short-term and population-averaged
claims.detail: The evidence base is strongest for average acute symptom response over weeks, and is less direct for long-term causal disease mechanisms or individual biological subtypes.

title: Cowan et al. PET study of serotonin release capacity in depression

claims.title: The study measured serotonin release capacity using PET imaging
claims.detail: The study used positron emission tomography methods to examine serotonin release capacity in people with depression compared with healthy controls.

claims.title: The study reported altered serotonin release capacity in depression
claims.detail: The study reported evidence consistent with reduced serotonin release capacity in a depressed group, contributing biological evidence relevant to serotonergic mechanisms.

claims.title: Imaging association alone does not establish causal primacy
claims.detail: A cross-sectional or case-control imaging difference can support biological involvement, but does not by itself prove whether the serotonin alteration is an initiating cause, consequence, compensation, subtype marker, or treatment-related feature.

title: Miller and Raison 2016 review of inflammation and depression

claims.title: Inflammation is associated with depressive symptoms in a subset of patients
claims.detail: The review summarizes evidence that inflammatory markers and immune activation are associated with depressive symptoms, with stronger relevance in some patient subgroups.

claims.title: Cytokines can affect neurotransmission, neuroendocrine function, and behavior
claims.detail: The review describes pathways through which cytokine signaling can influence monoamines, glutamate, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis function, sleep, motivation, and sickness-behavior-like symptoms.

claims.title: Inflammation evidence supports a causal pathway but not universal causation
claims.detail: The evidence supports inflammation as a plausible and sometimes causal contributor to depressive phenotypes, but does not show that all major depressive disorder is primarily caused by immune dysregulation.

claims.title: Interferon-alpha treatment can induce depressive symptoms
claims.detail: Clinical observations and studies of interferon-alpha treatment report that immune stimulation can induce depressive symptoms in a proportion of treated patients.

claims.title: Immune challenge provides temporally ordered causal evidence
claims.detail: Because immune activation precedes symptom development in interferon-treated patients, this evidence has stronger causal direction than ordinary cross-sectional inflammation-depression associations.

claims.title: Interferon-induced depression is a specific immune-challenge context
claims.detail: Depression emerging during interferon-alpha therapy is a medically induced immune-activation context and may not generalize directly to all spontaneous major depressive disorder.

title: Raison et al. 2013 infliximab trial in treatment-resistant depression

claims.title: Infliximab did not show overall superiority to placebo in the full sample
claims.detail: In a randomized trial of infliximab for treatment-resistant depression, the overall treatment effect in the full sample was not superior to placebo.

claims.title: Baseline inflammatory markers moderated treatment response
claims.detail: The trial reported that patients with higher baseline inflammatory markers, including elevated CRP, showed signals of better response to infliximab than patients without elevated inflammation.

claims.title: The trial supports inflammatory-subtype reasoning more than universal inflammation causation
claims.detail: The pattern is consistent with inflammation being important for a subgroup, while the negative overall result limits claims that blocking inflammation is broadly effective for all treatment-resistant depression.

title: Kohler et al. 2014 meta-analysis of anti-inflammatory treatment in depression

claims.title: Anti-inflammatory treatments showed antidepressant effects in pooled analyses
claims.detail: The meta-analysis reported that some anti-inflammatory treatments were associated with reductions in depressive symptoms across included randomized trials.

claims.title: The included interventions and populations were heterogeneous
claims.detail: The evidence included different anti-inflammatory agents, study designs, clinical populations, and baseline inflammation profiles.

claims.title: Meta-analytic symptom improvement does not identify a single primary cause
claims.detail: Pooled evidence of benefit from anti-inflammatory interventions supports immune involvement but does not prove that inflammation is the primary cause of depression in all patients.

title: Duman and Aghajanian 2012 synaptic dysfunction model of depression

claims.title: The review links depression to synaptic dysfunction and impaired plasticity
claims.detail: Duman and Aghajanian 2012 reviewed evidence that depression involves synaptic deficits, impaired neuroplasticity, and altered neural circuit function.

claims.title: Stress can reduce synaptic connectivity in mood-related circuits
claims.detail: The review describes animal and human evidence that chronic stress can reduce synaptic connections and alter prefrontal-limbic circuitry relevant to depressive behavior.

claims.title: Rapid-acting antidepressant effects are linked to synaptogenic signaling
claims.detail: The review discusses evidence that rapid antidepressant effects of agents such as ketamine involve glutamate signaling, mTOR-related pathways, and synaptic remodeling.

claims.title: Mechanistic convergence does not by itself prove first cause
claims.detail: Evidence that plasticity and synaptic function are altered in depression may identify a proximate mechanism or final common pathway, but does not alone prove that impaired plasticity is always the initiating cause.

title: Duman and Monteggia 2006 BDNF model of depression and treatment

claims.title: Stress and depression are associated with reduced BDNF-related signaling in some models
claims.detail: The review describes evidence that stress can reduce BDNF expression and neurotrophic support in brain regions implicated in depression.

claims.title: Antidepressant treatment can increase BDNF-related signaling
claims.detail: The review discusses evidence that chronic antidepressant treatment can increase BDNF expression or signaling pathways associated with neuroplasticity.

claims.title: BDNF effects vary by brain region and context
claims.detail: BDNF-related mechanisms can differ across brain regions and experimental contexts, limiting overly simple claims that depression is caused by globally low BDNF.

claims.title: Ketamine can produce rapid antidepressant effects
claims.detail: Randomized clinical studies report that ketamine can produce rapid reductions in depressive symptoms in some patients, including treatment-resistant depression.

claims.title: Ketamine evidence implicates glutamatergic and plasticity-related mechanisms
claims.detail: The rapid time course and mechanistic studies of ketamine support the relevance of glutamatergic signaling, synaptic remodeling, and plasticity-related pathways.

claims.title: Ketamine response does not prove plasticity impairment is the sole primary cause
claims.detail: A treatment effect through plasticity-related mechanisms can identify an effective intervention pathway without proving that impaired plasticity is the only or earliest cause of major depressive disorder.

title: HPA-axis and stress-circuit evidence in depression

claims.title: Stress-system dysregulation is observed in subsets of depression
claims.detail: Reviews report abnormalities of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis function and stress-response circuitry in some patients with depression.

claims.title: Early-life stress increases later depression risk
claims.detail: Longitudinal and epidemiological evidence links early-life adversity and chronic stress exposure to increased risk of later depressive disorders.

claims.title: Stress-circuit evidence bridges upstream exposure and downstream plasticity
claims.detail: Stress-system evidence can be interpreted as connecting environmental exposures to changes in neuroplasticity, inflammation, monoamine signaling, and mood-related circuit function.

title: Depression heterogeneity and precision psychiatry evidence

claims.title: Major depressive disorder is clinically and biologically heterogeneous
claims.detail: Reviews of depression heterogeneity emphasize that major depressive disorder contains diverse symptom profiles, trajectories, treatment responses, and biological correlates.

claims.title: One-mechanism explanations can overgeneralize across subtypes
claims.detail: Because depression is heterogeneous, a mechanism with strong evidence in one subgroup may be overgeneralized if presented as the universal primary cause for all depression.

claims.title: Biomarker-stratified designs are needed to compare causal hypotheses
claims.detail: Precision psychiatry approaches argue for stratifying patients by biomarkers, stress history, inflammatory status, treatment response, and neural measures to test mechanistic subtypes.
